item.title: Introduction
item.description: DevKitty UI is a UI standard library we’re building so anyone can write apps for our devices and conference badges. Every app built on it shares the same headers, footers, menus and popups, so apps look and feel consistent no matter who wrote them.

item.title: 🐈 Meet CutieCat
item.description:
❤️
If you have a v0 CutieCat, you’re an early supporter of the project! Your feedback & suggestions are cherished.



What is the CutieCat?

CutieCat is your new hacking & prototyping companion! It’s a cat-shaped console that lets you experiment with USB Attacks, Wireless Hacking, and fun mini-projects in CircuitPython.

item.title: Introduction
item.description: From time to time, a new exploit in ubiquitous hardware (like USB) is engendered. Taking advantage of such vulnerabilities often requires specialized knowledge, or is patched quickly enough that the attack surface is practically non-existent in real world applications.

item.title: API
item.description:
Screens

Every screen is a Screen subclass. You build its layout in onEnter, and repeat the same calls in onResume so the screen comes back correctly after a child screen closes.

item.title: Get Started
item.description:

Adafruit Circuitpython is a beginner-friendly language that runs directly on microcontrollers. This means instead of compiling & uploading code from your computer, you can run code directly on your DevKitty!

Overview

The ESP32-S2 is a capable chip that supports WiFi functionality, native USB, and a handful of other nifty features that make it perfect for powering our pocket-sized hacking companions.

item.title: 🖥️ Firmware Guide
item.description:
ℹ️
Our firmware is currently experimental as we continue to explore & make improvements to the DevKitty ecosystem.

CutieCat comes flashed with QA Firmware to test basic functionality. To start hacking you’ll have to load new firmware. If you’re adventurous you can even learn to write your own!

item.title: 🐈 CutieCat
item.description:
Overview

CutieCat is a modular cat-shaped console that supports Adafruit QT-Py & Seeed Studio Xiao style microcontrollers.

These tiny but powerful MCU’s support WiFi, Bluetooth, Native USB, and all the other fun hacking features we love, in a minimal footprint. CutieCats ship with the Xiao ESP32-S3 but you can easily swap in your own microcontroller!

item.title: Introduction
item.description:
What is Wardriving?

Wardriving is a reconaissance technique that involves driving around while scanning for wireless devices. It’s one of the quickest ways to gather intelligence on large amounts of WiFi networks and smart devices!

item.title: USB Attacks
item.description:
Why USB Attacks?

USB Attacks take advantage of physical access to an unlocked computer - if you have seconds of access to someone’s unattended machine, this is one of the most effective ways to compromise them!

item.title: ⚡ MiniMeter
item.description:
🛈
Skip ahead to the mods if you’re just looking to install your MiniMeter!

Overview

MiniMeter is a compact LiPo Charger & Battery Meter. The minimal footprint can be dropped into any existing design or easily powers microcontrollers! Every DevKitty design is compatible with MiniMeter.

item.title: Payload Guide
item.description: Our ScriptKitty Firmware supports DuckyScript™, making it easy to create your first payload! If you need inspiration, you can find a list of DuckyScrit payloads on the Hak5 GitHub repository.

item.title: Config
item.description: To edit the default WiFi network on ScriptKitty, or change the default USB device identifiers on ScriptKitty, you can simply edit the config.txt file on the flash drive! To reload the settings, simply restart your CutieCat!

item.title: Hardware
item.description:
What You Need

Wardriving combines wireless reconnaissance & location data - since DevKitty boards are already capable of sniffing WiFi & Bluetooth, this means all you need is a GPS module!

item.title: Live Control API
item.description:
The DevKitty supports live command both through a web interface and via a web API.

Web Interface

To access the web interface and run payloads live, connect to the DevKitty’s Wi-Fi access point and visit http://192.168.4.1/create.html

item.title: Wi-Fi Sniffing
item.description:
The DevKitty hardware can sniff Wi-Fi packets, allowing hackers to hunt for particular Wi-Fi devices or write packet filters to display deauthentication packets.

To get started, you’ll need to install CircuitPython on your DevKitty.
